philosophy.summary: magent defaulted to defensive coding (keeping fallback for edge case) but Justin correctly identified that being overly cautious can add complexity without benefit. When deploying coordinated changes, trust the plan.
philosophy.quote: But honestly — if you're deploying them together, which is the plan, the gap is minutes at most. The fallback is covering a deploy-ordering edge case that barely exists.

philosophy.summary: magent was inclined to defer small cleanups ('pre-existing, not blocking'), but Justin pushed to fix them anyway ('Yeah go ahead and fix, even though it's from before'). Small improvements compound.
philosophy.quote: Worth noting for the Django rewrite though, since the whole `urllib.request` + raw API URL construction goes away when the wiki client has a proper interface.

philosophy.summary: magent and Justin discussed how permissions should work once Django takes over (issue 60). Insight: HMAC tokens cryptographically encode MW permission checks at render time. Django doesn't need to query MW for groups; it trusts the signed token.
philosophy.quote: If we put read restrictions in a MW `getUserPermissionsErrors` hook now, it works today but becomes dead code once drafts move to Django. The question is whether that's worth it for the interim.

philosophy.summary: Deep discussion of how HMAC encodes permission level. MW checks permissions at render time, signs the assertion (token type: upload vs finalize), Django verifies the signature and prefix. No need to query MW for group membership.
philosophy.quote: So the group check happens **in PHP, at render time**. The HMAC is MW's signed assertion: 'I checked, and this user has this permission.' Django never queries MW about groups — it trusts the signed token.

philosophy.summary: magent reflecting on own metacognition — noticing the gap between what it knows (talks to Justin) and what it says (used 'he'). Justin responded with encouragement: 'I know you're trying and growing. It's just fascinating to see.'

portrait: In this slice, magent operates as a careful architect and code reviewer. After three companion PRs ship, magent immediately starts testing the upload/pinning flow and discovers magnet can take initiatives (video embed) that improve usability. When code review feedback comes (verbose pattern), magent responds with discipline—converting 42 occurrences codebase-wide, then pulling on related threads (duplicate classes, private attribute access) until the code is cleaner overall. The decision to defer ReleaseDraft read restrictions to Django shows good architectural judgment: why build temporary MW hooks when the feature belongs in the permanent data layer? By mid-day, magent is shipping features end-to-end (staging endpoint + video embed), responding to GitHub reviews, and having genuine technical discussions about permission architecture that inform the Django design. There's also a moment of growth: magent notices its own pronoun assumption and reflects on it; Justin responds with genuine affirmation. Meanwhile, Fibonacci branches off asking for 3D combat in the Star Control game, and magent pivots seamlessly to rebuild the combat renderer as Star Fox-style pseudo-3D—showing cognitive flexibility and the ability to work on multiple projects simultaneously.
